**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: default OAuth `state` is predictable**

```dart
String _randomState() =>
    DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toRadixString(16);
```

When the caller omits `state`, both this executor and the sync twin (`figma_sync_tools.dart:430`) fall back to a hex-encoded timestamp, which is trivially guessable — weakening the CSRF protection `state` exists for, and deviating from the Java implementation the doc references (`Long.toHexString(doubleToLongBits(random))`, i.e. random bits). Risk is low in a local CLI flow where the user pastes the code manually, but `Random.secure()` (or `Uuid`) costs one line and restores the intent:

```dart
final r = Random.secure();
String _randomState() =>
    List.generate(8, (_) => r.nextInt(256)).map((b) => b.toRadixString(16).padLeft(2, '0')).join();
```

## PR Description

## What changed

Ported the full Java `FigmaClient` `@MCPTool` surface (21 tools) to the Dart integration: OAuth2 flow (`figma_oauth2_get_auth_url` / `figma_oauth2_exchange_code`), `figma_me`, href-based structure/content tools (`get_file_structure`, `get_icons`, `get_layers`, `get_layers_batch`, `get_node_children`, `get_node_details`, `get_text_content`, `get_styles`, `render_nodes`, `get_image_fills`, downloads), team/project listings, and file comments — on both the async MCP path and the sync JS bridge. `figma_get_styles` now matches the Java stub (empty token envelope, keyed by `href`); `figma_test` returns the Java `me()` map shape. All 20 Figma names came off the `java_mcp_tool_gaps` ratchet; `figma_test`/`figma_get_styles` came off the `js_sync_surface_gaps` ratchet.

## Key decisions

- New pure modules shared by async + sync paths: `figma_url.dart` (URL parsing), `figma_document.dart` (JSON shaping: `findAllComponents`, layer summaries, text/styles/me envelopes), `figma_oauth.dart` (OAuth2 helpers), `figma_transfer.dart` (request shapes, 100-id batching, id caps, md5 download cache).
- Sync surface dispatches all 21 names via blocking curl through the existing `SyncToolDispatcher` prefix routing; Java-null results serialize as JSON `null`.
- Java quirks preserved deliberately: dashed vs colon node-id handling per tool, empty-map `{}` on `get_layers_batch` failure, id caps (10/20), render batching, md5-named image cache.
- `crypto` promoted from transitive to direct dependency (md5 cache naming, Java `getCachedFile` parity).
- ~90 new unit tests (URL/document/oauth/client/executor/sync); ratchet fixtures tightened (`java_mcp_tool_gaps`, `java_mcp_tool_params`, `java_mcp_param_drift`, `js_sync_surface_gaps`).

# gh-173: dmtools java dmtools dart alignment

## Description

Must be inline with java version https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/

dmtools-dart vs. Java dmtools (dm.ai) — parity gaps observed
High-level notes from evaluating dmtools-dart as a drop-in replacement for the Java dm.ai CLI. Shared for awareness / triage — not tied to any specific deployment or configuration.

1. Figma tool catalog uses a different, non-parity API surface
The Java tool has a specific set of figma_* MCP tools (e.g. figma_get_file_structure, figma_get_layers, figma_download_image_of_file, figma_list_team_projects, figma_list_project_files, figma_get_icons, etc.) that agent scripts and prompts invoke by exact name.

dmtools-dart's Figma integration instead exposes a different set of tool names (figma_get_file, figma_get_file_nodes, figma_get_node, figma_export_image, figma_get_components, figma_get_styles, ...). None of the names overlap with the Java catalog. Any script or prompt written against the Java Figma tool names will fail with a tool-not-found error under dmtools-dart today. This looks like the Figma integration was built against a generic Figma REST API shape rather than ported from the Java @MCPTool definitions.

2. Confluence tool catalog is partially mismatched
Some Confluence tools that exist in the Java catalog (e.g. confluence_search_content_by_text, confluence_content_by_title, confluence_find_or_create) are not present in dmtools-dart under those names. Similar-purpose tools exist under different names (e.g. confluence_search, confluence_content_by_id), but scripts/prompts written against the Java tool names would fail to resolve them.

3. Jira write-path behavior is not yet at full parity
Based on the project's own tracked parity ledger, several Jira write operations still differ from Java behavior — most notably around comment formatting (markdown is not yet converted to Jira's wiki markup the way the Java client does), label add/remove case-sensitivity handling, and some default field sets returned on ticket reads. jira_post_comment is the single most frequently invoked tool across agent scripts, so any formatting divergence there has outsized impact. Some related fixes (e.g. around jira_move_to_status error handling) appear to be landing incrementally.

4. GitHub/GitLab sync tool behavior is not yet at full parity
Per the same tracked ledger, a number of GitHub/GitLab sync behaviors are still open: PR comment ordering, HTTP redirect handling (e.g. for job logs), and non-2xx/pagination error semantics (some cases appear to silently return empty results instead of surfacing an error the way the Java client does).   - `FigmaSyncTools._getLayersBatch` — CRAP 14.08 (CC 4, 14% covered)

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

2. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT ×2 — `getLayers` parses href outside its failure guard** (async `figma_client.dart:320` and sync twin `figma_sync_tools.dart:316`): a URL without `node-id` throws `StateError` instead of returning the documented `null`, inconsistent with `getLayersBatch`/`getFileStructure` which parse inside their guards.

3. 💡 **SUGGESTION ×2**: predictable OAuth `state` fallback (hex timestamp vs Java's random bits, both paths), and the scrambled header comment block in `test/fixtures/js_sync_surface_gaps.txt` (looks like an accidental sort).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #186._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/integrations/figma/figma_client.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):
🚨 **BLOCKING: binary image downloads are corrupted on the async MCP path**

`downloadImage` fetches the image via `_http.getAbsolute(url)` (a `dio.get<String>`) and then re-encodes the decoded **String** back to bytes:

```dart
final body = await _http.getAbsolute(url);
file.writeAsBytesSync(utf8.encode(body), flush: true);
```

Dio's default transformer decodes any non-JSON response body with `utf8.decode(..., allowMalformed: true)` (verified in dio 5.11.1, `sync_transformer.dart` / `fused_transformer.dart`). Every byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 — starting with the `0x89` in the PNG magic header — is replaced by U+FFFD, and `utf8.encode` then writes `EF BF BD` instead of the original byte. Any real PNG/JPG downloaded through `figma_download_node_image`, `figma_download_image_of_file`, or `figma_download_image_as_file` on the async (`FigmaToolExecutor`) path is corrupted and will not open as an image.

The sync path is unaffected (`syncCurlStaged` streams raw bytes to the file), and the existing async tests only assert on the text mock `'PNG-DATA'`, so nothing catches this — including the byte-for-byte echo-server tests added in the rework, which exercise the curl path only.

Fix: fetch bytes instead of text and write them verbatim, e.g.:

```dart
// figma_http_client.dart
Future<List<int>> getAbsoluteBytes(String url) async {
  final response = await dio.get<List<int>>(
    url,
    options: Options(responseType: ResponseType.bytes),
  );
  return response.data ?? const [];
}

// figma_client.dart
file.writeAsBytesSync(await _http.getAbsoluteBytes(url), flush: true);
```

Keep `getAbsolute` (String) for `getSvgContent`, which is legitimately text. Add a regression test whose mock CDN returns bytes that are invalid UTF-8 (e.g. a real PNG header) and assert the cached file matches byte-for-byte.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/integrations/figma/figma_client.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>?> getLayers(String href) async {
  final target = figmaUrlNodeId(figmaCleanHref(href));  // throws StateError
  try {
    ...
```

`figmaUrlNodeId` calls `figmaExtractQueryParam`, which throws `StateError` when the URL has no `node-id`. Because that call sits *before* the `try`, a design URL without `node-id` — a perfectly valid input for the sibling tools (`getFileStructure`, `getIcons`, `getNodeDetails`, `getTextContent`, `getLayersBatch` all parse inside their guard and return `null`/`{}`) — escapes `getLayers` as an exception, contradicting the method's own dartdoc ("`null` when there are no children or on request failure (Java parity)").

On the MCP surface this propagates out of `FigmaToolExecutor`; on the JS surface the twin in `FigmaSyncTools._getLayers` (figma_sync_tools.dart:316) has the same shape, so the exception becomes a `Tool execution failed: ...` JS error instead of the Java `null`. Either move the extraction inside the `try`, or document/test the deviation from the Java swallow-and-return-null pattern and apply it consistently across `getLayers`, `getLayersBatch`, and `getNodeChildren`.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/js/sync_tools/figma_sync_tools.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: sync `_getLayers` extracts the URL before the guard**

```dart
final target = _urlNodeId(args);   // outside _guarded — throws on missing node-id
return _guarded(() { ... });
```

Same issue as the async twin (`FigmaClient.getLayers`): `_urlNodeId` throws `StateError` for an href without `node-id`, so the error escapes the `_guarded` wrapper and surfaces as a bridge-level `Tool execution failed` instead of the JSON `null` the handler returns for every other failure mode (and that `_getLayersBatch` returns as `{}` on parse failure). Move `_urlNodeId(args)` inside the `_guarded` closure — or, if Java genuinely rethrows here, align the async client and both doc comments to say so.

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/integrations/figma/figma_tools.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: default OAuth `state` is predictable**

```dart
String _randomState() =>
    DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toRadixString(16);
```

When the caller omits `state`, both this executor and the sync twin (`figma_sync_tools.dart:430`) fall back to a hex-encoded timestamp, which is trivially guessable — weakening the CSRF protection `state` exists for, and deviating from the Java implementation the doc references (`Long.toHexString(doubleToLongBits(random))`, i.e. random bits). Risk is low in a local CLI flow where the user pastes the code manually, but `Random.secure()` (or `Uuid`) costs one line and restores the intent:

```dart
final r = Random.secure();
String _randomState() =>
    List.generate(8, (_) => r.nextInt(256)).map((b) => b.toRadixString(16).padLeft(2, '0')).join();
```

  - `FigmaSyncTools._download` — CRAP 30.00 (CC 5, 0% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._getSvgContent` — CRAP 16.76 (CC 5, 22% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._getLayersBatch` — CRAP 14.08 (CC 4, 14% covered)

TDD red-green: first reproduced the failing gate locally, then added tests that exercise the uncovered branches over the existing Python `EchoServer` (the sync path blocks the isolate with curl, so a separate process must serve HTTP), and finally reduced complexity only where 100%/uncoverable-without-network code still breached the threshold. No Java-parity behavior was changed.

1. **Echo fixtures** (`test/js/test_echo_server.py`): new marker-routed fixtures `/figsvg/*` (render map → SVG body / 404), `/figdl/*` (render map → PNG bytes / 404), `/figlayers/v1/files/*/nodes` (per-id documents with one child; id `7:7` carries a null document to hit the skip branch).
2. **New tests** (`test/js/sync_tools/figma_sync_tools_test.dart`, 10 new):

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):

🚨 **BLOCKING: binary image downloads are corrupted on the async MCP path**

`downloadImage` fetches the image via `_http.getAbsolute(url)` (a `dio.get<String>`) and then re-encodes the decoded **String** back to bytes:

```dart
final body = await _http.getAbsolute(url);
file.writeAsBytesSync(utf8.encode(body), flush: true);
```

Dio's default transformer decodes any non-JSON response body with `utf8.decode(..., allowMalformed: true)` (verified in dio 5.11.1, `sync_transformer.dart` / `fused_transformer.dart`). Every byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 — starting with the `0x89` in the PNG magic header — is replaced by U+FFFD, and `utf8.encode` then writes `EF BF BD` instead of the original byte. Any real PNG/JPG downloaded through `figma_download_node_image`, `figma_download_image_of_file`, or `figma_download_image_as_file` on the async (`FigmaToolExecutor`) path is corrupted and will not open as an image.

The sync path is unaffected (`syncCurlStaged` streams raw bytes to the file), and the existing async tests only assert on the text mock `'PNG-DATA'`, so nothing catches this — including the byte-for-byte echo-server tests added in the rework, which exercise the curl path only.

```dart
// figma_http_client.dart
Future<List<int>> getAbsoluteBytes(String url) async {
  final response = await dio.get<List<int>>(
    url,
    options: Options(responseType: ResponseType.bytes),
  );
  return response.data ?? const [];
}

// figma_client.dart
file.writeAsBytesSync(await _http.getAbsoluteBytes(url), flush: true);
```

Keep `getAbsolute` (String) for `getSvgContent`, which is legitimately text. Add a regression test whose mock CDN returns bytes that are invalid UTF-8 (e.g. a real PNG header) and assert the cached file matches byte-for-byte.

# gh-173: dmtools java dmtools dart alignment

## Description

Must be inline with java version https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/

dmtools-dart vs. Java dmtools (dm.ai) — parity gaps observed
High-level notes from evaluating dmtools-dart as a drop-in replacement for the Java dm.ai CLI. Shared for awareness / triage — not tied to any specific deployment or configuration.

1. Figma tool catalog uses a different, non-parity API surface
The Java tool has a specific set of figma_* MCP tools (e.g. figma_get_file_structure, figma_get_layers, figma_download_image_of_file, figma_list_team_projects, figma_list_project_files, figma_get_icons, etc.) that agent scripts and prompts invoke by exact name.

dmtools-dart's Figma integration instead exposes a different set of tool names (figma_get_file, figma_get_file_nodes, figma_get_node, figma_export_image, figma_get_components, figma_get_styles, ...). None of the names overlap with the Java catalog. Any script or prompt written against the Java Figma tool names will fail with a tool-not-found error under dmtools-dart today. This looks like the Figma integration was built against a generic Figma REST API shape rather than ported from the Java @MCPTool definitions.

2. Confluence tool catalog is partially mismatched
Some Confluence tools that exist in the Java catalog (e.g. confluence_search_content_by_text, confluence_content_by_title, confluence_find_or_create) are not present in dmtools-dart under those names. Similar-purpose tools exist under different names (e.g. confluence_search, confluence_content_by_id), but scripts/prompts written against the Java tool names would fail to resolve them.

3. Jira write-path behavior is not yet at full parity
Based on the project's own tracked parity ledger, several Jira write operations still differ from Java behavior — most notably around comment formatting (markdown is not yet converted to Jira's wiki markup the way the Java client does), label add/remove case-sensitivity handling, and some default field sets returned on ticket reads. jira_post_comment is the single most frequently invoked tool across agent scripts, so any formatting divergence there has outsized impact. Some related fixes (e.g. around jira_move_to_status error handling) appear to be landing incrementally.

4. GitHub/GitLab sync tool behavior is not yet at full parity
Per the same tracked ledger, a number of GitHub/GitLab sync behaviors are still open: PR comment ordering, HTTP redirect handling (e.g. for job logs), and non-2xx/pagination error semantics (some cases appear to silently return empty results instead of surfacing an error the way the Java client does). Workflows that depend on exact PR/comment/pipeline behavior (review, rework, merge automation) are the most exposed to this gap.

5. Overall parity completion is still early relative to messaging
The project's own audit ledger (opened to track exhaustive Java-behavior parity, independent of the "phases complete" narrative) showed a small fraction of tracked items closed as of the last recorded session, even though the JS runtime, CLI plumbing, and the agent test suite are already in good shape. The gap is concentrated in fine-grained behavioral fidelity (exact error messages, field defaults, response shapes) rather than missing functionality — worth knowing before treating any given version as a byte-for-byte drop-in replacement for the Java CLI.

The Phase 6 "Java parity completion" audit (221 items, opened 2026-08-24 after an owner mandate for zero-deviation parity) was at score 13/221 as of the last logged session (2026-09-11) — despite the headline "all 5 phases implemented" framing.

# Rework: fix `quality` CI failure (gh-173)

## Issues/Notes

- Both `quality` checks failed on commit `a168bfe1`. No `ci_failures_full.log` was provided, so the failing step was reproduced locally by running the exact CI pipeline (`.github/workflows/quality.yml`): `dart format`, `dart analyze`, `dart test --coverage`, `coverage:format_coverage`, `crap4dart check --all`, `crap4dart analyze`.
- Root cause: **`crap4dart analyze` failed — Max CRAP 30.00 > threshold 8.00**. All six offenders were newly added Figma sync-path code with branches that had no test coverage (CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC):
  - `FigmaSyncTools._download` — CRAP 30.00 (CC 5, 0% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._getSvgContent` — CRAP 16.76 (CC 5, 22% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._getLayersBatch` — CRAP 14.08 (CC 4, 14% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._oauth2ExchangeCode` — CRAP 13.12 (CC 5, 31% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._downloadNodeImage` — CRAP 12.76 (CC 4, 18% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._downloadImageAsFile` — CRAP 10.75 (CC 4, 25% covered)
  - After the first coverage pass, `figmaMeResult` (CC 10, 100% covered → CRAP 10) and `_oauth2ExchangeCode` (still 26.7% covered) also breached the threshold; both fixed by behavior-preserving complexity extraction (see Approach).
- The pre-existing `class_size` warnings (26 violations, severity `warning`) are unchanged and do not fail the gate — no action taken, per the config's documented Java-parity rationale.

## Approach

TDD red-green: first reproduced the failing gate locally, then added tests that exercise the uncovered branches over the existing Python `EchoServer` (the sync path blocks the isolate with curl, so a separate process must serve HTTP), and finally reduced complexity only where 100%/uncoverable-without-network code still breached the threshold. No Java-parity behavior was changed.

1. **Echo fixtures** (`test/js/test_echo_server.py`): new marker-routed fixtures `/figsvg/*` (render map → SVG body / 404), `/figdl/*` (render map → PNG bytes / 404), `/figlayers/v1/files/*/nodes` (per-id documents with one child; id `7:7` carries a null document to hit the skip branch).
2. **New tests** (`test/js/sync_tools/figma_sync_tools_test.dart`, 10 new):
   - `figma_get_layers_batch`: dashed-id → colon-key mapping with trimming, null-document skip, 10-id request cap.
   - `figma_get_svg_content`: success, missing image URL → JSON `null`, failed fetch (404) → JSON `null`.
   - `figma_download_image_as_file`: download into the md5 cache (byte-for-byte), cache reuse on second call, download failure → JSON `null`; `figma_download_node_image`: success and no-URL cases. Cache dir is cleared per test so the curl branch runs deterministically.
   - `figma_oauth2_exchange_code`: missing-redirect-URI branch (the token POST targets the fixed `api.figma.com` URL and cannot be served by the echo server).
3. **Complexity extraction (behavior-preserving, verified by the existing full-branch tests):**
   - `figmaMeResult` → body handling split into `_figmaMeBodyResult` (CC 10 → 4/7, CRAP 4/7 at 100% coverage).
   - `_oauth2ExchangeCode` → guards split into `_oauth2CredentialsError` and the fixed-URL network half into `_oauth2Exchange` (main handler now 100% covered; network half CC 2 → CRAP 2·(1-0)³+2 = … ≤ 8 with headroom).

## Files Modified

- `test/js/test_echo_server.py` — Figma `/figsvg`, `/figdl`, `/figlayers` fixtures (gh-173).
- `test/js/sync_tools/figma_sync_tools_test.dart` — 10 new echo-server tests for `figma_get_layers_batch`, `figma_get_svg_content`, `figma_download_image_as_file`, `figma_download_node_image`, plus the missing-redirect-URI OAuth test; oversized test helpers split (`_testOauthUrlRouting`, `_downloadImageAsFileTests`, `_downloadNodeImageTests`) to satisfy the `method_size` gate.

- `lib/src/js/sync_tools/figma_sync_tools.dart` — `_oauth2ExchangeCode` split: `_oauth2CredentialsError` + `_oauth2Exchange` (no behavior change).

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

/// `figma_get_node_details`, `figma_get_text_content`, `figma_get_styles`,
/// `figma_get_layers*`, `figma_get_node_children`, `figma_list_*`,
/// `figma_get_file_comments`) plus the pre-existing Dart REST-shaped tools
/// (`figma_get_file`, `figma_get_file_nodes`, …) that predate the parity
/// port. The executor routes a tool name + arguments to the matching

      ..._discoveryTools(),

            'initial authorization code flow. Open the returned URL in a '
            'browser, authorize the app, and copy the code parameter from '
            'the redirect URL. Then call figma_oauth2_exchange_code to get '

        category: 'auth',

          ToolParam(
            name: 'redirectUri',

                'FIGMA_REDIRECT_URI env variable.',
            required: false,
          ),
          ToolParam(
            name: 'state',
            description: 'Random state string for CSRF protection',
            required: false,
          ),
          ToolParam(
            name: 'scope',
            description: 'Optional OAuth scope list (space-separated), e.g. '
                'file_content:read file_metadata:read. If omitted, uses '

            required: false,

        ],

        description: 'Exchanges a Figma OAuth2 authorization code for access '

            'figma_oauth2_get_auth_url. Store FIGMA_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN '
            'from the response in your dmtools.env to enable automatic '

        integration: 'figma',

Review complete. Outputs written to `outputs/` (valid JSON, 5 inline comments, all anchored to lines present in the diff).

## Verdict: `REQUEST_CHANGES` (1 blocking)

**Findings:**

1. 🚨 **BLOCKING — binary download corruption on the async MCP path** (`figma_client.dart:201`): `downloadImage` fetches via `dio.get<String>` and writes `utf8.encode(body)`. Verified against dio 5.11.1's transformer: non-JSON bodies are decoded with `utf8.decode(allowMalformed: true)`, so PNG/JPG bytes (starting with the `0x89` PNG magic) become U+FFFD and are re-encoded as `EF BF BD` — every binary file from `figma_download_node_image` / `figma_download_image_of_file` / `figma_download_image_as_file` is corrupted. The sync path (curl `-o`) is fine, and existing tests only assert on text mocks, so nothing catches it. Fix: `ResponseType.bytes` + write bytes verbatim, plus a binary regression test.

2. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT ×2 — `getLayers` parses href outside its failure guard** (async `figma_client.dart:320` and sync twin `figma_sync_tools.dart:316`): a URL without `node-id` throws `StateError` instead of returning the documented `null`, inconsistent with `getLayersBatch`/`getFileStructure` which parse inside their guards.

3. 💡 **SUGGESTION ×2**: predictable OAuth `state` fallback (hex timestamp vs Java's random bits, both paths), and the scrambled header comment block in `test/fixtures/js_sync_surface_gaps.txt` (looks like an accidental sort).

**Positives noted:** clean shared pure modules between async/sync paths, OAuth secrets staged via 0700 temp files (never in curl argv), no auth headers leaked to CDN fetches, thorough test coverage, and the rework demonstrably fixed the prior CRAP-gate CI failure.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. 🚨 **BLOCKING: binary image downloads are corrupted on the async MCP path**

`downloadImage` fetches the image via `_http.getAbsolute(url)` (a `dio.get<String>`) and then re-encodes the decoded **String** back to bytes:

```dart
final body = await _http.getAbsolute(url);
file.writeAsBytesSync(utf8.encode(body), flush: true);
```

Dio's default transformer decodes any non-JSON response body with `utf8.decode(..., allowMalformed: true)` (verified in dio 5.11.1, `sync_transformer.dart` / `fused_transformer.dart`). Every byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 — starting with the `0x89` in the PNG magic header — is replaced by U+FFFD, and `utf8.encode` then writes `EF BF BD` instead of the original byte. Any real PNG/JPG downloaded through `figma_download_node_image`, `figma_download_image_of_file`, or `figma_download_image_as_file` on the async (`FigmaToolExecutor`) path is corrupted and will not open as an image.

The sync path is unaffected (`syncCurlStaged` streams raw bytes to the file), and the existing async tests only assert on the text mock `'PNG-DATA'`, so nothing catches this — including the byte-for-byte echo-server tests added in the rework, which exercise the curl path only.

Fix: fetch bytes instead of text and write them verbatim, e.g.:

```dart
// figma_http_client.dart
Future<List<int>> getAbsoluteBytes(String url) async {
  final response = await dio.get<List<int>>(
    url,
    options: Options(responseType: ResponseType.bytes),
  );
  return response.data ?? const [];
}

// figma_client.dart
file.writeAsBytesSync(await _http.getAbsoluteBytes(url), flush: true);
```

Keep `getAbsolute` (String) for `getSvgContent`, which is legitimately text. Add a regression test whose mock CDN returns bytes that are invalid UTF-8 (e.g. a real PNG header) and assert the cached file matches byte-for-byte.

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>?> getLayers(String href) async {
  final target = figmaUrlNodeId(figmaCleanHref(href));  // throws StateError
  try {
    ...
```

`figmaUrlNodeId` calls `figmaExtractQueryParam`, which throws `StateError` when the URL has no `node-id`. Because that call sits *before* the `try`, a design URL without `node-id` — a perfectly valid input for the sibling tools (`getFileStructure`, `getIcons`, `getNodeDetails`, `getTextContent`, `getLayersBatch` all parse inside their guard and return `null`/`{}`) — escapes `getLayers` as an exception, contradicting the method's own dartdoc ("`null` when there are no children or on request failure (Java parity)").

On the MCP surface this propagates out of `FigmaToolExecutor`; on the JS surface the twin in `FigmaSyncTools._getLayers` (figma_sync_tools.dart:316) has the same shape, so the exception becomes a `Tool execution failed: ...` JS error instead of the Java `null`. Either move the extraction inside the `try`, or document/test the deviation from the Java swallow-and-return-null pattern and apply it consistently across `getLayers`, `getLayersBatch`, and `getNodeChildren`.

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/integrations/figma/figma_tools.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: default OAuth `state` is predictable**

```dart
String _randomState() =>
    DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toRadixString(16);
```

When the caller omits `state`, both this executor and the sync twin (`figma_sync_tools.dart:430`) fall back to a hex-encoded timestamp, which is trivially guessable — weakening the CSRF protection `state` exists for, and deviating from the Java implementation the doc references (`Long.toHexString(doubleToLongBits(random))`, i.e. random bits). Risk is low in a local CLI flow where the user pastes the code manually, but `Random.secure()` (or `Uuid`) costs one line and restores the intent:

```dart
final r = Random.secure();
String _randomState() =>
    List.generate(8, (_) => r.nextInt(256)).map((b) => b.toRadixString(16).padLeft(2, '0')).join();
```

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. TDD red-green: first reproduced the failing gate locally, then added tests that exercise the uncovered branches over the existing Python `EchoServer` (the sync path blocks the isolate with curl, so a separate process must serve HTTP), and finally reduced complexity only where 100%/uncoverable-without-network code still breached the threshold. `figmaUrlNodeId` calls `figmaExtractQueryParam`, which throws `StateError` when the URL has no `node-id`. Because that call sits *before* the `try`, a design URL without `node-id` — a perfectly valid input for the sibling tools (`getFileStructure`, `getIcons`, `getNodeDetails`, `getTextContent`, `getLayersBatch` all parse inside their guard and return `null`/`{}`) — escapes `getLayers` as an exception, contradicting the method's own dartdoc ("`null` when there are no children or on request failure (Java parity)").

On the MCP surface this propagates out of `FigmaToolExecutor`; on the JS surface the twin in `FigmaSyncTools._getLayers` (figma_sync_tools.dart:316) has the same shape, so the exception becomes a `Tool execution failed: ...` JS error instead of the Java `null`. Either move the extraction inside the `try`, or document/test the deviation from the Java swallow-and-return-null pattern and apply it consistently across `getLayers`, `getLayersBatch`, and `getNodeChildren`.

When the caller omits `state`, both this executor and the sync twin (`figma_sync_tools.dart:430`) fall back to a hex-encoded timestamp, which is trivially guessable — weakening the CSRF protection `state` exists for, and deviating from the Java implementation the doc references (`Long.toHexString(doubleToLongBits(random))`, i.e. random bits). Risk is low in a local CLI flow where the user pastes the code manually, but `Random.secure()` (or `Uuid`) costs one line and restores the intent:

```dart
final r = Random.secure();
String _randomState() =>
    List.generate(8, (_) => r.nextInt(256)).map((b) => b.toRadixString(16).padLeft(2, '0')).join();
```

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):

🚨 **BLOCKING: binary image downloads are corrupted on the async MCP path**

`downloadImage` fetches the image via `_http.getAbsolute(url)` (a `dio.get<String>`) and then re-encodes the decoded **String** back to bytes:

```dart
final body = await _http.getAbsolute(url);
file.writeAsBytesSync(utf8.encode(body), flush: true);
```

Dio's default transformer decodes any non-JSON response body with `utf8.decode(..., allowMalformed: true)` (verified in dio 5.11.1, `sync_transformer.dart` / `fused_transformer.dart`). Every byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 — starting with the `0x89` in the PNG magic header — is replaced by U+FFFD, and `utf8.encode` then writes `EF BF BD` instead of the original byte. Any real PNG/JPG downloaded through `figma_download_node_image`, `figma_download_image_of_file`, or `figma_download_image_as_file` on the async (`FigmaToolExecutor`) path is corrupted and will not open as an image.

```dart
// figma_http_client.dart
Future<List<int>> getAbsoluteBytes(String url) async {
  final response = await dio.get<List<int>>(
    url,
    options: Options(responseType: ResponseType.bytes),
  );
  return response.data ?? const [];
}

// figma_client.dart
file.writeAsBytesSync(await _http.getAbsoluteBytes(url), flush: true);
```

Keep `getAbsolute` (String) for `getSvgContent`, which is legitimately text. Add a regression test whose mock CDN returns bytes that are invalid UTF-8 (e.g. a real PNG header) and assert the cached file matches byte-for-byte.

Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. # gh-173: dmtools java dmtools dart alignment

## Description

Must be inline with java version https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/

dmtools-dart vs. Java dmtools (dm.ai) — parity gaps observed
High-level notes from evaluating dmtools-dart as a drop-in replacement for the Java dm.ai CLI. Shared for awareness / triage — not tied to any specific deployment or configuration.

1. Figma tool catalog uses a different, non-parity API surface
The Java tool has a specific set of figma_* MCP tools (e.g. figma_get_file_structure, figma_get_layers, figma_download_image_of_file, figma_list_team_projects, figma_list_project_files, figma_get_icons, etc.) that agent scripts and prompts invoke by exact name.

dmtools-dart's Figma integration instead exposes a different set of tool names (figma_get_file, figma_get_file_nodes, figma_get_node, figma_export_image, figma_get_components, figma_get_styles, ...). None of the names overlap with the Java catalog. Any script or prompt written against the Java Figma tool names will fail with a tool-not-found error under dmtools-dart today. This looks like the Figma integration was built against a generic Figma REST API shape rather than ported from the Java @MCPTool definitions.

2. Confluence tool catalog is partially mismatched
Some Confluence tools that exist in the Java catalog (e.g. confluence_search_content_by_text, confluence_content_by_title, confluence_find_or_create) are not present in dmtools-dart under those names. Similar-purpose tools exist under different names (e.g. confluence_search, confluence_content_by_id), but scripts/prompts written against the Java tool names would fail to resolve them.

3. Jira write-path behavior is not yet at full parity
Based on the project's own tracked parity ledger, several Jira write operations still differ from Java behavior — most notably around comment formatting (markdown is not yet converted to Jira's wiki markup the way the Java client does), label add/remove case-sensitivity handling, and some default field sets returned on ticket reads. jira_post_comment is the single most frequently invoked tool across agent scripts, so any formatting divergence there has outsized impact. Some related fixes (e.g. around jira_move_to_status error handling) appear to be landing incrementally.

4. GitHub/GitLab sync tool behavior is not yet at full parity
Per the same tracked ledger, a number of GitHub/GitLab sync behaviors are still open: PR comment ordering, HTTP redirect handling (e.g. for job logs), and non-2xx/pagination error semantics (some cases appear to silently return empty results instead of surfacing an error the way the Java client does). Workflows that depend on exact PR/comment/pipeline behavior (review, rework, merge automation) are the most exposed to this gap.

5. Overall parity completion is still early relative to messaging
The project's own audit ledger (opened to track exhaustive Java-behavior parity, independent of the "phases complete" narrative) showed a small fraction of tracked items closed as of the last recorded session, even though the JS runtime, CLI plumbing, and the agent test suite are already in good shape. The gap is concentrated in fine-grained behavioral fidelity (exact error messages, field defaults, response shapes) rather than missing functionality — worth knowing before treating any given version as a byte-for-byte drop-in replacement for the Java CLI.

The Phase 6 "Java parity completion" audit (221 items, opened 2026-08-24 after an owner mandate for zero-deviation parity) was at score 13/221 as of the last logged session (2026-09-11) — despite the headline "all 5 phases implemented" framing.

- Root cause: **`crap4dart analyze` failed — Max CRAP 30.00 > threshold 8.00**. All six offenders were newly added Figma sync-path code with branches that had no test coverage (CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC):
  - `FigmaSyncTools._download` — CRAP 30.00 (CC 5, 0% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._getSvgContent` — CRAP 16.76 (CC 5, 22% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._getLayersBatch` — CRAP 14.08 (CC 4, 14% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._oauth2ExchangeCode` — CRAP 13.12 (CC 5, 31% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._downloadNodeImage` — CRAP 12.76 (CC 4, 18% covered)
  - `FigmaSyncTools._downloadImageAsFile` — CRAP 10.75 (CC 4, 25% covered)
  - After the first coverage pass, `figmaMeResult` (CC 10, 100% covered → CRAP 10) and `_oauth2ExchangeCode` (still 26.7% covered) also breached the threshold; both fixed by behavior-preserving complexity extraction (see Approach).
- The pre-existing `class_size` warnings (26 violations, severity `warning`) are unchanged and do not fail the gate — no action taken, per the config's documented Java-parity rationale.

## Approach

TDD red-green: first reproduced the failing gate locally, then added tests that exercise the uncovered branches over the existing Python `EchoServer` (the sync path blocks the isolate with curl, so a separate process must serve HTTP), and finally reduced complexity only where 100%/uncoverable-without-network code still breached the threshold. No Java-parity behavior was changed.

1. **Echo fixtures** (`test/js/test_echo_server.py`): new marker-routed fixtures `/figsvg/*` (render map → SVG body / 404), `/figdl/*` (render map → PNG bytes / 404), `/figlayers/v1/files/*/nodes` (per-id documents with one child; id `7:7` carries a null document to hit the skip branch).

3. **Complexity extraction (behavior-preserving, verified by the existing full-branch tests):**

   - `_oauth2ExchangeCode` → guards split into `_oauth2CredentialsError` and the fixed-URL network half into `_oauth2Exchange` (main handler now 100% covered; network half CC 2 → CRAP 2·(1-0)³+2 = … ≤ 8 with headroom).

## Files Modified

- `test/js/test_echo_server.py` — Figma `/figsvg`, `/figdl`, `/figlayers` fixtures (gh-173).
- `test/js/sync_tools/figma_sync_tools_test.dart` — 10 new echo-server tests for `figma_get_layers_batch`, `figma_get_svg_content`, `figma_download_image_as_file`, `figma_download_node_image`, plus the missing-redirect-URI OAuth test; oversized test helpers split (`_testOauthUrlRouting`, `_downloadImageAsFileTests`, `_downloadNodeImageTests`) to satisfy the `method_size` gate.
- `lib/src/integrations/figma/figma_document.dart` — `figmaMeResult` split: `_figmaMeBodyResult` (no behavior change).
- `lib/src/js/sync_tools/figma_sync_tools.dart` — `_oauth2ExchangeCode` split: `_oauth2CredentialsError` + `_oauth2Exchange` (no behavior change).

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

## Verdict: `REQUEST_CHANGES` (1 blocking)

**Findings:**

1. 🚨 **BLOCKING — binary download corruption on the async MCP path** (`figma_client.dart:201`): `downloadImage` fetches via `dio.get<String>` and writes `utf8.encode(body)`. Verified against dio 5.11.1's transformer: non-JSON bodies are decoded with `utf8.decode(allowMalformed: true)`, so PNG/JPG bytes (starting with the `0x89` PNG magic) become U+FFFD and are re-encoded as `EF BF BD` — every binary file from `figma_download_node_image` / `figma_download_image_of_file` / `figma_download_image_as_file` is corrupted. The sync path (curl `-o`) is fine, and existing tests only assert on text mocks, so nothing catches it. Fix: `ResponseType.bytes` + write bytes verbatim, plus a binary regression test.

2. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT ×2 — `getLayers` parses href outside its failure guard** (async `figma_client.dart:320` and sync twin `figma_sync_tools.dart:316`): a URL without `node-id` throws `StateError` instead of returning the documented `null`, inconsistent with `getLayersBatch`/`getFileStructure` which parse inside their guards.

3. 💡 **SUGGESTION ×2**: predictable OAuth `state` fallback (hex timestamp vs Java's random bits, both paths), and the scrambled header comment block in `test/fixtures/js_sync_surface_gaps.txt` (looks like an accidental sort).

**Positives noted:** clean shared pure modules between async/sync paths, OAuth secrets staged via 0700 temp files (never in curl argv), no auth headers leaked to CDN fetches, thorough test coverage, and the rework demonstrably fixed the prior CRAP-gate CI failure.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Ported the full Java `FigmaClient` `@MCPTool` surface (21 tools) to the Dart integration: OAuth2 flow (`figma_oauth2_get_auth_url` / `figma_oauth2_exchange_code`), `figma_me`, href-based structure/content tools (`get_file_structure`, `get_icons`, `get_layers`, `get_layers_batch`, `get_node_children`, `get_node_details`, `get_text_content`, `get_styles`, `render_nodes`, `get_image_fills`, downloads), team/project listings, and file comments — on both the async MCP path and the sync JS bridge. `figma_get_styles` now matches the Java stub (empty token envelope, keyed by `href`); `figma_test` returns the Java `me()` map shape. # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #186._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/integrations/figma/figma_client.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):
🚨 **BLOCKING: binary image downloads are corrupted on the async MCP path**

`downloadImage` fetches the image via `_http.getAbsolute(url)` (a `dio.get<String>`) and then re-encodes the decoded **String** back to bytes:

```dart
final body = await _http.getAbsolute(url);
file.writeAsBytesSync(utf8.encode(body), flush: true);
```

Dio's default transformer decodes any non-JSON response body with `utf8.decode(..., allowMalformed: true)` (verified in dio 5.11.1, `sync_transformer.dart` / `fused_transformer.dart`). Every byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 — starting with the `0x89` in the PNG magic header — is replaced by U+FFFD, and `utf8.encode` then writes `EF BF BD` instead of the original byte. Any real PNG/JPG downloaded through `figma_download_node_image`, `figma_download_image_of_file`, or `figma_download_image_as_file` on the async (`FigmaToolExecutor`) path is corrupted and will not open as an image.

The sync path is unaffected (`syncCurlStaged` streams raw bytes to the file), and the existing async tests only assert on the text mock `'PNG-DATA'`, so nothing catches this — including the byte-for-byte echo-server tests added in the rework, which exercise the curl path only.

Fix: fetch bytes instead of text and write them verbatim, e.g.:

```dart
// figma_http_client.dart
Future<List<int>> getAbsoluteBytes(String url) async {
  final response = await dio.get<List<int>>(
    url,
    options: Options(responseType: ResponseType.bytes),
  );
  return response.data ?? const [];
}

// figma_client.dart
file.writeAsBytesSync(await _http.getAbsoluteBytes(url), flush: true);
```

Keep `getAbsolute` (String) for `getSvgContent`, which is legitimately text. Add a regression test whose mock CDN returns bytes that are invalid UTF-8 (e.g. a real PNG header) and assert the cached file matches byte-for-byte.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/integrations/figma/figma_client.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `getLayers` parses the href outside its failure guard**

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>?> getLayers(String href) async {
  final target = figmaUrlNodeId(figmaCleanHref(href));  // throws StateError
  try {
    ...
```

`figmaUrlNodeId` calls `figmaExtractQueryParam`, which throws `StateError` when the URL has no `node-id`. Because that call sits *before* the `try`, a design URL without `node-id` — a perfectly valid input for the sibling tools (`getFileStructure`, `getIcons`, `getNodeDetails`, `getTextContent`, `getLayersBatch` all parse inside their guard and return `null`/`{}`) — escapes `getLayers` as an exception, contradicting the method's own dartdoc ("`null` when there are no children or on request failure (Java parity)").

On the MCP surface this propagates out of `FigmaToolExecutor`; on the JS surface the twin in `FigmaSyncTools._getLayers` (figma_sync_tools.dart:316) has the same shape, so the exception becomes a `Tool execution failed: ...` JS error instead of the Java `null`. Either move the extraction inside the `try`, or document/test the deviation from the Java swallow-and-return-null pattern and apply it consistently across `getLayers`, `getLayersBatch`, and `getNodeChildren`.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/js/sync_tools/figma_sync_tools.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: sync `_getLayers` extracts the URL before the guard**

```dart
final target = _urlNodeId(args);   // outside _guarded — throws on missing node-id
return _guarded(() { ... });
```

Same issue as the async twin (`FigmaClient.getLayers`): `_urlNodeId` throws `StateError` for an href without `node-id`, so the error escapes the `_guarded` wrapper and surfaces as a bridge-level `Tool execution failed` instead of the JSON `null` the handler returns for every other failure mode (and that `_getLayersBatch` returns as `{}` on parse failure). Move `_urlNodeId(args)` inside the `_guarded` closure — or, if Java genuinely rethrows here, align the async client and both doc comments to say so.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/integrations/figma/figma_tools.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: default OAuth `state` is predictable**

```dart
String _randomState() =>
    DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toRadixString(16);
```

When the caller omits `state`, both this executor and the sync twin (`figma_sync_tools.dart:430`) fall back to a hex-encoded timestamp, which is trivially guessable — weakening the CSRF protection `state` exists for, and deviating from the Java implementation the doc references (`Long.toHexString(doubleToLongBits(random))`, i.e. random bits). Risk is low in a local CLI flow where the user pastes the code manually, but `Random.secure()` (or `Uuid`) costs one line and restores the intent:

```dart
final r = Random.secure();
String _randomState() =>
    List.generate(8, (_) => r.nextInt(256)).map((b) => b.toRadixString(16).padLeft(2, '0')).join();
```

---

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4.
